Hi Markus,

Quick context: HelioCloud is planning a staged public launch of our conversational search product in Q3. We expect initial traffic concentrated in NA and EU with APAC ramping 6-8 weeks after GA. Attached is the MAU/peak concurrency forecast (heliocloud_mau_forecast.xlsx).

As part of procurement we need:
- A preliminary dedicated pool sizing recommendation for US, EU and APAC (preferred GPU families and node counts).
- Expected cold-start and steady-state p99 token latency targets for a 1.6k token avg prompt size.
- An outline of the canary approach (length, traffic % for pilot).
- Contract/PO timeline to align with our internal procurement (we're targeting PO by 2027-05-15).

Key constraints: we want predictable unit cost and the option to burst on shared capacity for non-critical batch jobs. Also need clarity on data residency for EU and Singapore.

Can you put together a ballpark sizing and timeline this week? Happy to jump on a 30-min call if helpful.

Thanks,
Carlos

Markus — initial sizing and assumptions below. I kept numbers conservative to preserve latency SLOs and allow room for growth during the canary.

Assumptions:
- Average prompt length: 1.6k tokens (customer provided)
- Model family: recommending H100-85GB + H100-96GB for production (better perf for long contexts), offer A100-80GB as cost-saving fallback for EU test pool.
- Steady-state concurrency: use customer's peak concurrency from spreadsheet + 25% buffer for burst.

Proposed initial pools (canary phase, 60-day pilot):
- US (us-west): 8 H100 nodes (sustained throughput ~480 tok/s aggregate, p99 ~ 180-220ms for 1.6k tokens)
- EU (frankfurt): 6 H100 nodes (p99 ~ 200-240ms)
- APAC (singapore): 4 H100 nodes in warm standby, auto-burst to shared pool for initial GA (p99 targeted 220-260ms)

Cost/ops notes:
- H100 vs A100: H100 pool ~20-30% higher per-token infra cost but reduces risk of p99 regressions on long-context workloads. Call this out as a configurable tradeoff in the SOW.
- KV/prefix caching: enable regional prefix cache for EU and US to cut token cost ~15% for repeated queries.
- Autoscaling: configure sustained window + burst lanes for non-API batch jobs to hit cost targets.

Procurement & timeline:
- Draft SOW + initial pricing by 2027-02-18 (Rachel to draft).
- Commercial review and redlines: 2 weeks after SOW shared.
- Target PO submission: 2027-05-10 to leave padding for procurement.

Attachments: I drafted a quick SOW redline (SOW_redline_v1.pdf) — Rachel, please iterate on the residency + rollback language.

Next steps/action items:
- Lauren: share a short capacity appendix with exact node counts and throughput calculations (I will attach to customer).
- Rachel: publish SOW draft by EOD 2/18.
- Karthik: confirm regional capacity availability with infra (H100 inventory for April/May).

—Lauren
Head of Dedicated Accounts
Redwood Inference

Carlos — thanks for the forecast and for the call earlier. Per our internal review, we recommend the following initial commercial proposal and operational plan (high level):

Executive summary (short):
- Initial committed pools: US 8 H100 nodes; EU 6 H100 nodes; APAC 4 H100 nodes on warm standby with auto-burst to shared capacity.
- Canary: 60–90 day canary starting at ~10% production traffic for 2 weeks, then ramp to 40% for 30 days before full GA. Rollback triggers: sustained p99 > 350ms for more than 30m or error-rate > 2%.
- Timeline: SOW delivered by 2027-02-18 (attached link). Commercial redlines complete by 2027-03-04. Target PO by 2027-05-10.

Operational asks for HelioCloud:
- Confirm target p99 latency gate for your UX (we assumed <=250ms initially).
- Provide origins/ingress regions for traffic (helps with routing lanes).
- PO contact and billing entity for EU residency clauses.

We will include cost deltas in the SOW for an A100 fallback if you prefer lower unit cost. Rachel attached the SOW redline and a short appendix with math. Karthik will follow up on H100 inventory and tentative allocation windows for April/May.

If this looks good I can push a formal SOW via DocuSign and set up a technical onboarding call to lock in the canary dates.

Best,
Markus Klein
VP, Sales — Dedicated
Redwood Inference
